# RU-direct: Russian sites bypass the VPN

Goal: while the VPN is on, requests to Russian sites/services leave **directly from the user's device and
address**; everything else (including foreign services) goes through the VPN as before
(client → entry node (RU) → hop2 → foreign exit node).

The split is done **on the client**, before traffic enters the tunnel. That is the only place where "directly
from the user" is possible: once a packet is in the tunnel it can at best exit from the RU node, never from the
user's own address.

## Dataset (`internal/rudirect/data`, generated by `tools/ru-direct/gen.py`)

* RU set = ipverse RU GeoIP (same snapshot as `mobilecore/ru_bypass.go`) ∪ every ip2asn range whose origin
  ASN is registered in RU (catches RU services announced from foreign space). Private/special ranges and the
  tunnel resolvers (8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4, 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1) are never direct.
* Prefixes of key RU services (Yandex, VK/Mail.ru, Sber, T-Bank, Ozon, WB, Avito, Госуслуги, banks, Kaspersky,
  Rutube, Kinopoisk, 2GIS, HH, NSPK, …) are always kept.
* `ru-direct-v4.txt` — direct list (Windows, Android 13+): RU prefixes up to /20 + key services + RU
  CDN/anti-DDoS/hosting (Qrator, ServicePipe, StormWall, DDoS-Guard, NGENIX, CDNVideo, EdgeCenter, Selectel,
  Timeweb, Beget, Cloud.ru, …). 3106 prefixes, 86% of RU address space.
* `ru-direct-complement.txt` — Android < 13 tunnel list (IPv4 minus direct set; RU up to /18 + key services).
  3307 prefixes, 65% of RU space. CDN/hosting is *not* direct here (coarser budget).
* Budgets keep the route tables small; anything dropped simply stays in the VPN (safe direction).

Validation (snapshot 2026-10): 51/52 popular RU services direct on Windows/Android 13+ (33/52 on Android < 13);
0/16 foreign services (Google, YouTube, Telegram, Instagram, X, ChatGPT, GitHub, Discord, …) direct.

Regenerate (needs the iptoasn.com dump):

    python3 tools/ru-direct/gen.py --ip2asn ip2asn-v4.tsv.gz --out internal/rudirect/data
    go test ./internal/rudirect

The same files are packaged into the APK (`android/app/build.gradle`, `assets.srcDirs`) and embedded into the
Windows broker (`//go:embed`), so both clients always use one dataset. Rebuild/release both after regenerating.

## Android (4.6.0, `RuDirect.kt`, `ChamVpnService.establishTun`)

* Android 13+: `addRoute(0.0.0.0/0)` + `excludeRoute()` for every direct prefix.
* Android 6–12: no exclusion API → only the complement list is routed into the VPN.
* DNS stays 8.8.8.8 inside the tunnel (the prebuilt mobilecore AAR cannot steer DNS; sending all DNS to a RU
  resolver would leak foreign lookups and expose them to ISP DNS tampering). Russian services mostly answer with
  RU addresses regardless of resolver location; a RU name that resolves to a foreign CDN edge just uses the VPN.
* If the platform rejects the route set (e.g. OEM Binder limits) the session falls back to the full tunnel and
  logs `ru-direct routes rejected`.
* Setting: «Протокол» → «Российские сайты напрямую» (default on; change while disconnected). Stored in the
  encrypted vault as `ru_direct`.

## Windows (4.6.0, `cmd/chamd/rudirect_windows.go`)

* `setupRoutes`: after the node bypass, before the capture routes, the direct prefixes are installed through the
  physical default route (iphlpapi `CreateIpForwardEntry2`, metric 6, protocol NETMGMT, active store only).
  Removed in `removeRoutes`; stale rows (metric 6 + our prefix) are purged on the next connect.
* DNS: questions for Russian domains (`rudirect.IsRussianDomain`) → Yandex DoH `common.dot.dns.yandex.net`
  at 77.88.8.8 (itself a direct prefix) so geo-CDNs return RU edges. Everything else → existing in-tunnel
  resolver. Any failure → in-tunnel resolver.
* IPC: `{"command":"connect",…,"ru_direct":false}` disables the split; absent = on.
* UI: «Протокол» → «Российские сайты напрямую» (preferences.json `RuDirect`).

## Limitations / not done

* IPv4 only (IPv6 is blocked by both clients anyway).
* GeoIP/ASN based: a RU site hosted abroad (Cloudflare, AWS, Hetzner…) goes through the VPN; a small foreign
  site hosted in a RU data centre goes directly. Refresh the dataset every 1–3 months.
* No server-side fallback on the entry node (RU) ("RU traffic exits from the RU node") — no access to that node
  from build-host. It would be an extra safety net for traffic that slipped into the tunnel, not a replacement.
* Needs acceptance on real devices: Android 13+ and < 13 (route count acceptance by OEM builds), Windows 10/11
  (route install, DNS steering), then signing/publishing through the usual release scripts.
